# swarm-equivalence — capture procedure (#5273, ADR-5273 implementation step 1)

This directory will hold the representative fixtures for the swarm equivalence gate. It is empty
on purpose. Per [`../README.md`](../README.md), a gate's fixtures may not be written by the gate's
author, so every file here must come from a **real run**, captured by a person, not generated by
the code under test or by whoever wrote it.

Until the captures land, `tests/swarm.test.cjs` and `tests/swarm-anchors.test.cjs` pin the
mechanics only. The assertions that read this directory (structural equivalence with the
single-agent artefacts, and "rejects the fabricated anchor by name") are added with the captures.

## What to capture

Pick one real phase of a real project on Claude Code, with a `CONTEXT.md`, at least three
source files to review, and research worth doing. Then run it twice.

### Run A — single-agent (swarm off)

```bash
gsd-tools config-set swarm.enabled false
```

Plan the phase (`/gsd-plan-phase <n>`), execute it, and let code review run. Copy:

| From the phase directory | To here |
|---|---|
| `<NN>-CONTEXT.md` | `CONTEXT.md` |
| `<NN>-RESEARCH.md` | `single/RESEARCH.md` |
| `<NN>-PATTERNS.md` | `single/PATTERNS.md` |
| `<NN>-REVIEW.md` | `single/REVIEW.md` |

### Run B — swarm on

Reset the phase artefacts (keep `CONTEXT.md`), then:

```bash
gsd-tools config-set swarm.enabled true
```

Run the same phase again and copy the three artefacts to `swarm/`, plus `<NN>-SWARM.json` to
`swarm/SWARM.json`. Run this headless (`claude -p`) so every dispatch's token figure is
host-reported; an estimate in the evidence fails ADR-5273 Decision 5.

### The negative fixture — a real fabricated anchor

The raw worker answers exist on disk only as the `--answers` file the spawn site hands to
`gsd-tools swarm check-answers`. ADR-5273 step 4 makes the spawn site write that file into the
phase directory (`<NN>-SWARM-ANSWERS-<role>.json`), so it survives the run; until step 4 lands there
is nothing to copy. From run B, find one answer in that file whose quote does not match its cited
lines (Haiku-class workers produce these; that is the point of the check) and save that entry
verbatim as `fabricated-worker-answer.json`. Do not edit it, and do not write one by hand: a
fabricated anchor written by the gate's author tests the author's idea of a mistake, not the
model's.

If run B produced none, say so in this README with the run date; do not substitute one.

## MANIFEST.json

Add it with the captures, in the shape the other gates use (`file → source → gate → expected`).
Name the project, phase, date and GSD version of each run in a `source` field.
